articles.headline: Chamoli Tunnel Disaster Toll Reaches Eight With Two Workers Still Missing
articles.summary: Rescue workers recovered another body from the inundated Chamoli tunnel in Uttarakhand, bringing the confirmed death toll to eight. The incident occurred when an aquifer burst during construction, flooding the site. Two workers remain missing. Officials from the THDC and district administration are using high-power pumps to drain water and locate the remaining trapped personnel.

articles.headline: PM Warns Of Dimaagi Naxals As Opposition Criticizes Independence Day Speech
articles.summary: Prime Minister Modi warned against 'dimaagi Naxals' or intellectual Naxals who he claimed are misguiding the youth and hindering national progress. The Congress party hit back, accusing the PM of using a national platform to attack political opponents and suppress dissent. Opposition leaders argued the term is used to silence critics and ignore pressing issues like unemployment.

articles.headline: Saket Building Collapse: Police Charge Owner And Builders For Negligence
articles.summary: Delhi Police filed a chargesheet against the owner and two builders involved in the fatal building collapse in Saket's Saidulajab. Six people died in the incident. The accused face charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder and negligent conduct. Investigations revealed the structure used sub-standard materials and lacked necessary municipal clearances for construction.

articles.headline: Master Plan 2047 Targets Widespread Revamp For Delhi’s Karol Bagh
articles.summary: Under the Master Plan for Delhi-2047, the Karol Bagh area is set for an extensive redevelopment focus. The project includes upgrading dilapidated buildings, enhancing green spaces, and improving pedestrian infrastructure in the commercial hub. The plan aims to balance high-density residential needs with modernized retail zones while preserving the area’s historical character.

articles.headline: Karnataka Deputy CM Unveils AI And Coding Programs For State Schools
articles.summary: Deputy CM DK Shivakumar launched the 'Gaurav' and 'Coding Gurukula' initiatives aimed at introducing artificial intelligence and computer coding to Karnataka's government schools. The programs will start for students from Class 6 onwards to prepare them for global competition. The state government intends to partner with major tech firms to develop curriculum and provide training modules.

articles.headline: PM Modis Target For India To Reach Top Five Global Banks
articles.summary: Prime Minister Modi set a goal for at least one Indian bank to be among the world's top five financial institutions within a decade. This is part of the broader 'Viksit Bharat' roadmap which also aims to place 50 Indian companies in the Fortune 500. The strategy involves scaling domestic banking operations and increasing the global presence of Indian financial services.

articles.headline: India To Develop Modern Civil Defence Network Against New Age Threats
articles.summary: The Union government announced plans to create a Modern Civil Defence Network to protect critical infrastructure from hybrid warfare. This includes defenses against cyberattacks on power grids and financial systems, as well as drone threats. The network will be integrated with local administrations across 400 districts and involves training citizens in emergency response and rescue.

articles.headline: CJI Says Legal Profession Was Instrumental In India's Freedom Movement
articles.summary: Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud stated that the legal profession found its 'natural place' in the Indian independence movement. Addressing the Supreme Court Bar Association, he highlighted how lawyers were at the forefront of challenging colonial laws and protecting civil liberties. He urged current legal practitioners to maintain this legacy by upholding constitutional values and justice.

articles.headline: Delhi CM Gupta Emphasizes Capital's Special Role In Viksit Bharat Mission
articles.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta stated that the national capital will lead India's transformation into a developed nation. She announced a series of infrastructure projects, including three new metro corridors and the redevelopment of 12,000 km of roads. She also highlighted schemes for women's safety and free public transport for transgender individuals as key components of social progress.

articles.headline: Delhi Police Bust Human Trafficking Racket And Rescue Rescued Infant
articles.summary: The Delhi Police dismantled an interstate human trafficking syndicate that specialized in the sale of infants. Five individuals were arrested following a tip-off at Yamuna Bazar. Investigators rescued an infant who was allegedly sold for ₹4 lakh. The gang targeted economically weaker families and facilitated illegal adoptions through forged documents and a network of middlemen.

articles.headline: Delhi Government To Roll Out New Semiconductor And Drone Policies
articles.summary: The Delhi government is finalizing new policies for the semiconductor and drone industries to attract investment and create jobs. The drone policy aims to foster an ecosystem for delivery services, infrastructure mapping, and agriculture. The semiconductor policy focuses on assembly and testing (OSAT) units. Both drafts are expected to be presented for public feedback by late September.

articles.headline: Jharkhand Protesters Demand CM Hemant Sorens Resignation Over JPSC Irregularities
articles.summary: Hundreds of students and job aspirants protested in Ranchi, demanding the resignation of Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren. The protesters alleged widespread irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) exams. They called for a high-level inquiry into paper leaks and unfair selection processes. The state government denied the charges, stating that all recruitments were transparent.

articles.headline: ITBP DIG And Driver Killed In Road Accident In Uttar Pradesh
articles.summary: A Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) and his driver were killed when their vehicle collided with a truck on the Dehradun-Paon-Sahib highway. The accident occurred during heavy rainfall and low visibility. Senior police officials confirmed the deaths and stated that a preliminary investigation into the collision has been launched.

articles.headline: Bombay High Court Quashes FIR Against Former Axis Mutual Fund Dealer
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court quashed a First Information Report (FIR) filed against Viresh Kanani, a former chief dealer of Axis Mutual Fund. The court ruled that the allegations of front-running did not constitute an offense under the Indian Penal Code sections cited. It noted that such matters fall under the jurisdiction of SEBI regulations and do not automatically invite criminal prosecution.

articles.headline: Bengal Temples In Focus As Architects Trace Brick Architecture Evolution
articles.summary: A new architectural study highlights the unique 17th-century terracotta and brick temples of West Bengal. Researchers identified over 1,000 such structures featuring domes, arches, and intricate carvings that blend local and European styles. The study emphasizes the urgent need for conservation efforts to protect these vulnerable monuments from monsoon damage and urban encroachment.

articles.headline: Taliban Marks Five Years Of Rule In Afghanistan With Military Parade
articles.summary: The Taliban celebrated five years since their takeover of Afghanistan with a large military parade at the former US Bagram airbase. The event showcased captured US military hardware and homegrown drones. Despite internal celebrations, the international community continues to withhold formal recognition due to the Taliban's restrictive policies on women's education and human rights.

articles.headline: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty Ready For Home Tournament Return
articles.summary: India's star badminton duo Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty announced they are fully fit and ready for the India Indoors Championship. Following a period of injury management, the world number 5 pair is eyeing a title at home to regain momentum. They emphasized the importance of home support and their target to qualify for the season-ending World Tour Finals.

articles.headline: Better.com CEO Vishal Garg fired over losses and poor judgment
articles.summary: The board of Better Home & Finance has terminated CEO Vishal Garg, citing concerns over his judgment, temperament, and credibility. Garg gained notoriety in 2021 for firing 900 employees via a single Zoom call. The company has seen stock prices plummet by 90% and losses exceed $1.5 billion since 2022. Harinder Singh will lead as interim CEO.

articles.headline: US pulls aircraft carrier from Asia as Trump shifts focus
articles.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln is leaving the Middle East and Asia, leaving the region without a US aircraft carrier for the first time in months. The move comes as President Trump focuses on domestic priorities and potential tensions with Iran. Navy officials expressed concerns over the prolonged deployment's impact on sailor morale and ship maintenance.

articles.headline: Govt announces tax amnesty scheme for undisclosed foreign assets
articles.summary: The Indian government has introduced a new voluntary disclosure scheme for non-resident Indians (NRIs) and students abroad to declare previously undisclosed foreign assets and income. Participants must pay a 31% tax and a 60% penalty to avoid further prosecution. The scheme aims to track black money and will remain open until December 31, 2026.

articles.headline: Cambridge professor Jason Arday found dead after plagiarism allegations
articles.summary: Jason Arday, 41, who became the youngest Black professor at Cambridge University, was found dead at his home following intense scrutiny over plagiarism allegations. Arday had resigned his post after an investigation found substantial overlaps between his work and previously published studies. Friends described him as a 'gentle man' who felt targeted by a 'public and brutal' campaign.

articles.headline: Environmental disaster as oil leaks from Russian tanker off Oman
articles.summary: A major oil leak has been detected from the Russian tanker Caroline Bezengi near Al-Qibliyah Island off the coast of Oman. The vessel, reportedly carrying Russian crude, was abandoned after an explosion. While no direct link to regional conflict is confirmed, environmentalists warn of a massive threat to local marine life and coastal ecosystems.

articles.headline: PM Rahman of Bangladesh to visit India next week
articles.summary: Bangladesh's Prime Minister Rahman is scheduled to visit New Delhi next week for bilateral talks with PM Narendra Modi. This follows an invitation sent through National Security Advisor Ajit Doval. The discussions are expected to cover border management, domestic political stability in Dhaka, water-sharing agreements, and trade normalization between the neighbors.

articles.headline: Three suspected poachers killed in shootout at Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary
articles.summary: Foresters killed three men during a night-time encounter in the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka. Officials claim the men were armed poachers who opened fire when challenged. However, local villagers allege the deceased were farmers who had entered the forest to retrieve lost cattle. Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has ordered a magisterial probe into the incident.

articles.headline: Karnataka proposes jail terms for rallies held without prior permission
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has proposed a new bill that mandates up to three years of imprisonment and heavy fines for organizers of public rallies or protests conducted without official approval. The Regulation of Use of Government Premises and Public Property Bill, 2026, aims to prevent public nuisance but faces criticism for potentially stifling democratic dissent.

articles.headline: Emission test fees hiked across Karnataka for all vehicle types
articles.summary: The Karnataka transport department has increased Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) charges. Testing fees for two-wheelers have risen from ₹65 to ₹80, four-wheelers (petrol/CNG) from ₹75 to ₹110, and diesel vehicles from ₹160 to ₹200. The revision, the first since 2022, aims to help testing centers cope with rising operational costs and equipment maintenance.

articles.headline: Karnataka CM promises 72,000 jobs and new AI university
articles.summary: In his Independence Day address, CM Siddaramaiah announced plans to fill 72,000 government vacancies and establish a dedicated Artificial Intelligence (AI) university in Bengaluru. He also unveiled the 'Udyoga Setu' portal to link job seekers with industry requirements and promised to focus on green infrastructure and sustainable urban development for the capital city.

articles.headline: Bengaluru Metro skips stops as massive crowds disrupt Independence Day
articles.summary: Surging crowds celebrating Independence Day at Vidhana Soudha forced the Bengaluru Metro (BMRCL) to skip several key stations, including Cubbon Park and Dr. BR Ambedkar Station, to manage platform congestion. Train services were temporarily suspended at peak times for safety reasons. Commuters faced significant delays as thousands turned out for the 'Freedom Habba' festivities.

articles.headline: Clarence High suspends offline classes as 500 students fall ill
articles.summary: Clarence High School in Bengaluru has moved to online classes for two weeks after over 500 students reported symptoms of fever, cold, and cough. Two cases of H1N1 (swine flu) have been confirmed. School management blamed unhygienic street food vendors near the campus for the outbreak and has requested city authorities to clear unauthorized stalls for student safety.

articles.headline: Dead viper found on Vande Bharat seat sparks passenger panic
articles.summary: Passengers on the Ernakulam Junction-KSR Bengaluru Vande Bharat Express were left in shock after a dead viper was found on a seat in the C6 coach. The incident occurred shortly before arrival at Bengaluru. While railway officials claimed the snake was likely planted as a 'hoax' or act of sabotage, passengers have raised serious concerns regarding onboard safety and cleaning protocols.

articles.headline: Mass psychogenic illness spooks Maharashtra school as 608 girls flee
articles.summary: Over 600 students fled a tribal-dominated government ashram school in Amravati, Maharashtra, after several girls experienced fits of uncontrollable laughing and crying. Medical experts have identified the phenomenon as mass psychogenic illness, triggered by rumors of ghosts and poor living conditions. Officials and rationalists are working to counsel students and counter local superstitions.

articles.headline: PM Modi makes fresh pitch for Women’s Reservation Bill
articles.summary: Prime Minister Modi has called on opposition parties to support the implementation of the Women’s Reservation Bill. Despite being passed in 2023, the bill's implementation depends on a new census and delimitation exercise. Modi urged parties to move beyond 'dishonest pitches' and ensure 33% representation for women in Parliament and state assemblies starting from the 2029 polls.

articles.headline: PM Modi sets vision for 'Viksit Bharat' with seven streams of strength
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi outlined seven 'streams of strength' to drive India toward becoming a developed nation by 2047. Key goals include making India a global manufacturing hub, achieving 100 GW of nuclear power capacity, and launching a nationwide campaign to identify sports talent among children aged 5 to 15. He emphasized self-reliance in defense and green energy.

articles.headline: India to remain among fastest growing economies says SBI report
articles.summary: An SBI research report predicts India will remain a top-growing economy with 8% GDP growth in Q1 FY25. The study highlights strong capital inflows, robust corporate performance, and a monsoon recovery as key drivers. Foreign investment is showing a 'reversing trend' with inflows of $52.3 billion mobilized under various RBI schemes to support the rupee and economy.

articles.headline: India Inc Q1 earnings surprise despite significant cost pressures
articles.summary: Corporate India reported a surprising 21% year-on-year growth in net profit for Q1 FY25 across 4,220 companies. While revenue growth was modest at 8%, sectors like banking, automotive, and pharmaceuticals showed resilience. However, the refinery and cement sectors faced margin pressure due to higher material costs and marketing losses on fuel retail.

articles.headline: AIIMS debars two syringe suppliers over patient safety concerns
articles.summary: AIIMS Delhi has debarred Tirupati Medilines and Life-O-Line Technologist for supplying defective syringes and suction sets. The action follows repeated complaints of broken needles, fungal contamination, and leakage, which posed severe risks to patients in critical care units. The firms were disqualified from future procurement for up to two years.

articles.headline: Small taxpayers can now disclose foreign assets under new I-T scheme
articles.summary: The Income Tax Department has introduced a scheme for small taxpayers to disclose overlooked foreign assets worth up to ₹5 crore. Announced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, the scheme provides immunity from prosecution under the Black Money Act for disclosures made by December 31, 2026. A 30% tax and 10% penalty apply to the disclosed amounts.

articles.headline: Flat Nifty reveals a wide performance divide among mutual funds
articles.summary: Analysis of 449 equity mutual funds shows a sharp divergence in performance over the last two years despite a flat Nifty index. While Nifty 50 delivered just 1.7% returns, several mid-cap and small-cap funds achieved over 15% CAGR. The data highlights that active fund management and sector rotation were crucial for generating alpha in a sideways market.

articles.headline: Strong balance sheets provide India Inc with new financial freedom
articles.summary: Indian corporations have significantly improved their financial health over the last five years, with debt-to-equity ratios at multi-year lows. This resilience, particularly in the auto and steel sectors, allows companies to shift from survival mode to aggressive capital expenditure. Improved interest coverage ratios suggest businesses are well-placed for the next phase of investment.

articles.headline: Post-filing ITR checklist: Steps to ensure smooth tax processing
articles.summary: Following the ITR filing deadline, taxpayers are advised to complete a post-filing checklist to avoid delays or penalties. Essential steps include verifying the return within 30 days via Aadhaar OTP, tracking Section 143(1) intimations, and reconciling tax credits with Form 26AS. Errors can be corrected through revised returns under Section 139(5) before December 31.

articles.headline: Jane Street reports first monthly trading slump in a decade
articles.summary: Proprietary trading giant Jane Street recorded a monthly loss in July, its first in ten years, amid high market volatility. The firm, which saw over $40 billion in net trading revenue earlier this year, suffered from unsuccessful bets in Asian equity markets. Despite the setback, the firm is proceeding with a $14.6 billion bond deal to overhaul its debt stack.

articles.headline: Horizon Industrial Parks IPO: High valuation leaves little room for upside
articles.summary: Blackstone-backed Horizon Industrial Parks is launching its IPO with a valuation that analysts find expensive. The company, which operates Grade-A warehouses, has an enterprise value-to-EBITDA multiple of 31.3x. While the logistics sector shows strong growth potential due to e-commerce, the high asking price and debt levels suggest investors should exercise caution.

articles.headline: Gaja Alternative Asset Management IPO brings private equity to public markets
articles.summary: Gaja Alternative Asset Management's ₹550-crore IPO marks a rare public offering by a pure-play alternative asset manager. The firm manages four funds focused on mid-market growth sectors. While the company has a credible track record and diversified revenue streams from management fees and carried interest, investors are advised to monitor the sustainability of its recurring income.

articles.headline: Lalithaa Jewellery IPO: Analysts suggest waiting for better profitability clarity
articles.summary: Lalithaa Jewellery's ₹1,100-crore IPO is priced at a market cap of ₹11,500 crore. While the retailer has a strong presence in South India and ambitious expansion plans, analysts note high inventory levels and a recent sharp rise in gold prices that could impact margins. The company intends to use the proceeds for new stores and general corporate purposes.

articles.headline: Gold and silver prices expected to soften in the short term
articles.summary: Precious metals may face downward pressure in the coming week after failing to break key resistance levels. Gold is expected to find support around ₹1,47,000, while silver could see a retreat toward ₹2,25,000. Traders are advised to monitor US economic data and potential profit-booking, which could trigger a marginal correction in domestic prices.

articles.headline: New RBI rules shield borrowers in default from recovery agent harassment
articles.summary: The RBI has issued sweeping new guidelines to protect retail customers from aggressive debt recovery practices, effective January 2027. Recovery agents are strictly prohibited from contacting borrowers before 8 AM or after 7 PM, using abusive language, or making anonymous threats. Lenders remain fully accountable for the conduct of third-party recovery agencies they hire.

articles.headline: PM Modi targets 50 Indian companies entering the Fortune 500 list
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi set an ambitious target to see 50 Indian companies join the Fortune 500 list, up from the current nine. Speaking at the Red Fort, he urged the nation's businesses to scale up and become global leaders. He also expressed a desire for an Indian bank to rank among the world's top financial institutions to support the growing economy.

articles.headline: Tata Trusts governance dispute raises concerns ahead of Tata Sons AGM
articles.summary: A legal dispute over the management of Tata Trusts has surfaced as Tata Sons prepares for its 108th Annual General Meeting. The Maharashtra Charity Commissioner is reviewing concerns regarding the selection of trustees and the influence of principal shareholders on the board. The outcome could impact the long-term governance structure of India's largest industrial conglomerate.

articles.headline: PhonePe leads UPI market with 10.86 billion transactions in July
articles.summary: PhonePe processed 10.86 billion UPI transactions in July, capturing a 48.3% market share by volume and 43.3% by value. Google Pay and Paytm followed in second and third place, respectively. Overall UPI transaction counts increased to 14.44 billion despite fewer business days in the month, signaling continued growth in India's digital payment ecosystem.

articles.headline: 1,000 days of Red Sea crisis continue to squeeze Indian exports
articles.summary: The ongoing Red Sea shipping crisis, now lasting over 1,000 days, continues to impact Indian trade through higher freight costs and delayed shipments. Exporters in sectors like textiles, chemicals, and auto components are facing margin pressure as they divert cargo around the Cape of Good Hope. This detour adds roughly 15-20 days to transit times for European and US markets.

articles.headline: India Plans 5 to 8 New Semiconductor Plants Within Eight Years
articles.summary: PM Modi announced that India aims to add five to eight more semiconductor manufacturing facilities over the next seven to eight years. The goal is to build a complete domestic supply chain to ensure national security and economic independence. This follows the approval of nine plants under the $15 billion India Semiconductor Mission, including facilities by Micron and Tata Electronics.

articles.headline: Tata Teleservices Succession Case Challenges Corporate India Continuity Plans
articles.summary: A leadership transition at Tata Teleservices has highlighted the complexities of succession planning in major Indian firms. Following Ratan Tata's exit, the board's decision-making process is under scrutiny regarding readiness for sudden departures. Experts suggest many large conglomerates remain vulnerable due to a lack of clear pipelines for internal talent and external recruitment.

articles.headline: AI-led Matchmaking Apps Attract Significant Venture Capital Investor Interest
articles.summary: Startups using artificial intelligence to refine user profiling for dating and marriage are drawing high investor interest. Firms like Knot.dating and Wavelength are raising millions to replace traditional swiping with AI-driven compatibility conversations. This shift comes as traditional dating platforms face stagnant growth and user fatigue with superficial matching processes.

articles.headline: Car Buyers Shift Toward CNG and EVs as Petrol Share Declines
articles.summary: Retail car sales in major Indian states show a growing preference for CNG, hybrids, and electric vehicles over traditional petrol engines. In July, petrol's market share dropped to 40.59% compared to 41.68% the previous year. High fuel costs and environmental concerns are driving consumers toward alternative powertrains, with E20 fuel compatibility becoming a key factor for new buyers.

articles.headline: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat Urges Raising Public Interest Issues Forcefully
articles.summary: Speaking at an Independence Day event in Nagpur, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat emphasized that opposition and protests on issues of public interest are necessary for a healthy democracy. He stated that while different viewpoints should be respected, concerns regarding demographic shifts and national strength must be addressed through dialogue and, when needed, peaceful public movements.

articles.headline: Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina Expected to Visit India for Diplomatic Talks
articles.summary: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is likely to visit India next week for a two-day trip to discuss energy, power, and water-sharing agreements. The visit aims to reset bilateral ties and address long-standing issues like the Teesta water treaty. New Delhi has invited her as part of an outreach to neighbors, signaling a focus on regional stability and infrastructure cooperation.

articles.headline: Alibaba Qwen AI Beats Google and Meta With 3 Billion Downloads
articles.summary: Alibaba Group’s Qwen AI models have surpassed 3 billion downloads in six months, eclipsing download figures for models from Meta and Google. The open-source Qwen family includes over 460 models used by developers worldwide. The success signals China's growing influence in the global AI landscape, as enterprises seek high-performance alternatives to restricted US-based AI technologies.

articles.headline: Investors Fund AI Talent Acquisition for Tech Startups Facing Gap
articles.summary: As the demand for specialized AI talent in India outstrips supply, venture capital firms are directly funding the recruitment of engineers for their portfolio companies. There is an estimated shortfall of 50,000 AI security engineers and 30,000 AI evaluation experts. Salaries for generative AI roles have surged by 24-27% year-on-year, prompting investors to step in to bridge the gap.

articles.headline: Govt Plans September Launch for PNG Drive 3.0 to Boost Adoption
articles.summary: The Indian government is preparing to launch the third phase of its piped natural gas (PNG) drive in September. The initiative aims to add 100,000 new connections daily to reduce reliance on imported LPG and traditional fuels. Despite global supply chain disruptions, the Ministry of Petroleum is pushing City Gas Distribution companies to expand infrastructure in urban residential areas.

articles.headline: Manipur Rivals Oppose Proposed Border Land Swap With Myanmar
articles.summary: Meitei and Kuki-Zo community groups in Manipur have temporarily united to oppose a proposed 3.5 sq km land swap with Myanmar in the Chandel district. The groups fear the loss of ancestral territory and believe the move could further destabilize the border. The Ministry of External Affairs acknowledged that certain sections of the India-Myanmar border remain under active discussion.

articles.headline: CBDT Opens One-Time Window to Declare Undisclosed Foreign Assets
articles.summary: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has announced a limited window for taxpayers to declare previously undisclosed foreign income and assets up to ₹5 crore. By paying a ₹1 lakh fee and applicable taxes, individuals can regularize their filings and avoid heavy penalties. The move is part of the government’s efforts to curb black money and improve transparency in foreign holdings.

articles.headline: Micro Diners See Surge in Demand for Exclusive Culinary Experiences
articles.summary: Tiny restaurants with fewer than 20 seats, known as 'micro-diners', are witnessing massive demand across Indian cities. These chef-led establishments offer intimate, reservation-only dining that focuses on storytelling and regional authenticity. The trend reflects a shift in consumer preference toward exclusivity and artisanal food, with patrons willing to wait weeks for a table.

articles.headline: Indian Tanker Crew Stranded 75 Days in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Captain Raman Kapoor and his 23-member crew recount their 75-day ordeal anchored in the Strait of Hormuz during an active war zone. Facing missile attacks and fuel shortages, the crew of the merchant vessel was caught in geopolitical crossfire. The story highlights the extreme risks faced by seafarers and the lack of international corridors for commercial ships in conflict zones.

articles.headline: Indian Film Classics Restored for Top Global International Festivals
articles.summary: For the first time, four restored Indian film classics have been selected for major international festivals, including Cannes and TIFF. Projects like 'Amma Ariyan' and 'Apur Sansar' have been digitally revitalized by the Film Heritage Foundation. This marks a significant milestone for Indian cinema preservation, showcasing the country’s rich film history to a global modern audience.

articles.headline: Attacks on Ships in Hormuz Mount as US Threatens Iran
articles.summary: Geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz have intensified, with 65 vessel incidents reported and 17 seafarer deaths. The US has vowed new economic measures against Iran to stop maritime aggression. As a vital passage for 20% of global oil, the instability has caused crude prices to rise, sparking fears of a prolonged energy supply disruption and global economic impact.

articles.headline: Belgium Wildfire Destroys 1,600 Hectares in One of Largest Blazes
articles.summary: A massive wildfire in Belgium has ravaged over 1,600 hectares of a national park near the German border. Hundreds of firefighters and aerial support units are battling the blaze, which was exacerbated by high winds and dry conditions. Residents in nearby Wallonia have been evacuated. Authorities describe it as one of the largest fires the country has faced in decades.

articles.headline: BWF World Badminton Championships Return to India After 17 Years
articles.summary: India is set to host the BWF World Badminton Championships after a 17-year hiatus. The event showcases the evolution of Indian badminton, with stars like PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen competing on home soil. The tournament features top global talent from China, Korea, and Japan, highlighting India's growing status as a premier destination for international racquet sports.

articles.headline: CAG flags major lapses in Green India Mission
articles.summary: CAG report highlights significant shortcomings in the Green India Mission (GIM) including inadequate funding, weak coordination, poor monitoring, and failure to meet forest cover and quality targets. The mission, part of India's climate plan, showed a 91.87% shortfall in improving forest quality and 97.57% shortfall in increasing forest cover.

articles.headline: NASA invites ISRO to participate in Moon Base program
articles.summary: NASA has invited ISRO to join its 'Moon Base' program near the Moon's south pole, part of the Artemis Accords. This initiative aims to build humankind's first outpost on a celestial body, around 2030, and involves significant private industry participation.

articles.headline: CJI expresses confidence in young lawyers
articles.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, in his Independence Day address at the Supreme Court, expressed confidence in young law graduates, highlighting their resilience, social awareness, and commitment to justice.

articles.headline: Farmers, police clash in Haryana over I-Day protest
articles.summary: Six Haryana Police personnel and numerous protesters were injured in Hansi during clashes. Farmers were marching against an Independence Day event, demanding arrests in a murder case.

articles.headline: Eighth body recovered from flooded Chamoli tunnel
articles.summary: Rescuers recovered an eighth body from a flooded tunnel in Chamoli, Uttarakhand, where 22 workers were trapped. Two workers remain missing from the hydroelectric project site.

articles.headline: Delhi CM urges youth to focus on nation-building, warns of 'urban Naxals'
articles.summary: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta urged youth to utilize skills for innovation and nation-building, warning against "urban Naxals." She stated India fights a "two-and-a-half-front war" including "a front within," and pledged to develop Delhi into a model 'active, attentive, attractive' city.

articles.headline: L-G Sandhu calls for collective effort to build 'Viksit Delhi'
articles.summary: Delhi L-G Taranjit Singh Sandhu urged residents, government, and civic bodies to collaborate for a 'Viksit Delhi,' balancing heritage with modernity. He highlighted priorities like cleaning Yamuna, tackling pollution, ensuring housing and healthcare, and safety.

articles.headline: Delhi citizens reflect on freedom, equality, and progress
articles.summary: Delhi citizens at Red Fort reflected on the meaning of freedom, citing progress in infrastructure and technology, but also expressing unease over discrimination, online trolling, and inequality, questioning if all feel truly free.

articles.headline: Kejriwal praises Gen Z for fighting for rights and basic facilities
articles.summary: AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal praised Gen Z and Gen Alpha for questioning governments and demanding rights, calling it "true freedom." He highlighted protests by children for better school facilities in various states.

articles.headline: PM's youth-focused I-Day announcements receive mixed reactions
articles.summary: PM Modi's Independence Day announcements on AI skilling and free online coaching for youth received praise from many attendees. However, some expressed skepticism, questioning the benefits' reach and raising concerns about paper leaks.

articles.headline: Delhi Speaker, DU V-C lead I-Day celebrations
articles.summary: High-ranking officials and dignitaries in Delhi, including Assembly Speaker Vijender Gupta and Delhi University Vice-Chancellor Yogesh Singh, marked Independence Day at their respective offices.

articles.headline: Three girls die of snakebite in tribal school, raises infrastructure concerns
articles.summary: Three girls died and three others were injured from a snakebite at a tribal residential school in Dhanora, Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, raising questions about the lack of medical infrastructure, ambulance access, and road network in the remote area.

articles.headline: Odisha govt. orders probe into firm’s water discharge into Baitarani river
articles.summary: Odisha government ordered a probe into a private power generation company's alleged discharge of excess water into the Baitarani river without informing authorities, amid floods in Keonhjar district.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi meets Ankita Bhandari's parents, alleges BJP 'protecting VIP'
articles.summary: Rahul Gandhi met Ankita Bhandari's parents, criticizing the BJP for allegedly protecting a "VIP" in the 2022 murder case. He accused BJP of a "warped mentality" for defending rapists and criminals.

articles.headline: Akhilesh Yadav warns SP leaders against controversial statements
articles.summary: SP president Akhilesh Yadav cautioned party leaders against making statements the BJP could exploit, emphasizing adherence to party guidelines after senior leader Shivpal Singh Yadav's controversial remarks.

articles.headline: Sanjay Raut questions delay in Women’s Reservation Act implementation
articles.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut urged PM Modi to explain why the Women's Reservation Act, passed in 2023, has not been implemented yet, advocating for power transfer to younger generations.

articles.headline: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari promises to restore State’s 'old glory'
articles.summary: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari, in his maiden Independence Day speech, pledged to restore Bengal's "old glory," focusing on job creation, women empowerment, and improving law and order.

articles.headline: Three minor sisters electrocuted to death in Rajasthan
articles.summary: Three minor sisters from a tribal family died from electrocution in Fatehpur village, Baran, Rajasthan, after touching an air cooler in their hut.

articles.headline: Police use water cannons on Hawara supporters marching to Governor's residence
articles.summary: Chandigarh police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse protesters seeking the release of Sikh prisoners, including Jagtar Singh Hawara, during a march towards Punjab Governor's residence.

articles.headline: Kuldeep Bishnoi supports Rao Inderjit Singh, warns BJP against ignoring seniors
articles.summary: Senior BJP leader Kuldeep Bishnoi backed Union Minister Rao Inderjit Singh's criticism of excluding local leaders from an event, warning that ignoring senior leaders could weaken the party.

articles.headline: Telangana electoral roll revision leaves 94 lakh voters uncertain
articles.summary: After draft electoral rolls are published on August 17, Telangana's EROs have 60 days to conduct hearings for 94 lakh voters whose details were unmapped or had logical discrepancies, raising concerns about the feasibility of the process.

articles.headline: The Hindu launches Tamil YouTube channel ‘The Hindu 360’
articles.summary: The Hindu Group Publishing Private Limited (THGPPL) launched ‘The Hindu 360,’ a Tamil YouTube channel, aiming to reach more Tamil users with investigative journalism and diverse content.

articles.headline: Uncertainty over PRC acceptance for Karnataka voter verification
articles.summary: Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer is yet to clarify if Permanent Residential Certificates (PRCs) will be accepted for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter verification, affecting 28 lakh 'unmapped' voters.

articles.headline: Kerala CM warns against communalism, advocates open-minded democracy
articles.summary: Kerala CM V.D. Satheesan warned against communalism, advocating for a democracy founded on open-mindedness, tolerance, and debate. He criticized insults based on caste and untouched the 'Vande Mataram' rendition mandate.

articles.headline: Three students injured in ABVP-NSUI clash at Hyderabad EFLU
articles.summary: A clash between ABVP and NSUI members at Hyderabad's EFLU campus resulted in three students sustaining serious head injuries. Police have booked cases against 14 students, arresting seven.

articles.headline: Man arrested for harassment in A.P., taken to court on foot by police
articles.summary: A man was arrested in Annamayya district, A.P., for harassing a woman and attempting to attack her with a sickle. Police took him to court on foot, and he was remanded for 14 days.

articles.headline: Karnataka HC: Caste abuses by politicians carry graver indignity
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court stated that casteist abuses by politicians in public carry a "graver indignity," emphasizing that the "poison of caste" still finds expression among those in power.

articles.headline: Telangana aims for ₹1-trillion economy by 2034: CM Revanth Reddy
articles.summary: Telangana CM A. Revanth Reddy announced the state aims for a $1-trillion economy by 2034, with per capita income reaching ₹4,18,931 in 2025-26. He also outlined plans to develop 'Bharat Future City' as India's first net-zero smart city.

articles.headline: Karnataka to create 1 lakh jobs, boost AI education: Shivakumar
articles.summary: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar announced plans to create one lakh new jobs, expand AI education, and establish technology hubs statewide. The government also targets filling 72,000 key vacancies.

articles.headline: Youth can become burden without jobs, skills: Mohan Bhagwat
articles.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat warned that India's youth, while a demographic dividend, could become a societal burden if not properly equipped with jobs and skills. He emphasized India needs its own distinct development strategy.

articles.headline: Ranchi students hold 'Tiranga Yatra' on day 22 of protest; CM Soren vows 'systemic change'
articles.summary: Hundreds of Jharkhand students protested alleged exam irregularities with a 'Tiranga Yatra' on day 22. CM Hemant Soren promised "systemic change" and a transparent, time-bound exam calendar. Protesters demand CBI inquiry and exam cancellations.

articles.headline: JLKM leader Devendra Mahto alleges assault by Ranchi police
articles.summary: JLKM leader Devendra Nath Mahto, on hunger strike over exam irregularities, alleged Ranchi police assaulted him and his associates, injuring his chest, when he tried to join a 'Tiranga Yatra.'

articles.headline: Odisha CM Majhi alleges 'external forces' behind Gen Z protest
articles.summary: Odisha CM Mohan Charan Majhi reiterated that "external forces" were behind the Gen Z protest critical of the BJP government's education policy, asserting PM Modi would not compromise national interests.

articles.headline: CJP founder launches 'School theek karo' campaign for education reform
articles.summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke launched the "School theek karo" (fix the school) campaign, highlighting dilapidated government schools and staff shortages, starting in Maharashtra and Rajasthan.

articles.headline: PM Modi's 'dimagi Naxals' remark draws Opposition criticism
articles.summary: Opposition parties criticized PM Modi's "dimagi Naxals" remark, calling it an attempt to stigmatize dissent. Leaders like Mallikarjun Kharge and Jairam Ramesh accused him of targeting those questioning the government.

articles.headline: Maharashtra CM Fadnavis backs PM Modi’s 'intellectual Naxals' remark
articles.summary: Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis seconded PM Modi's "intellectual Naxals" remark, saying while armed Naxalism is defeated, ideological Naxalism poses a dangerous threat. He criticized the Congress over the Vande Mataram controversy.

articles.headline: U.P. CM Adityanath rolls out new 'Youth Policy' for 'Viksit Bharat'
articles.summary: Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath announced a new 'Youth Policy' focusing on skill, innovation, and employment to transform the state's demographic dividend into a development engine for 'Viksit Bharat'.

articles.headline: Global leaders greet India on I-Day, reaffirm bilateral ties
articles.summary: India's global partners, including France, Russia, Australia, and the U.S., extended Independence Day greetings, reaffirming commitment to strengthening bilateral ties and regional cooperation.

articles.headline: Amit Shah hails PM's I-Day speech as 'Viksit Bharat' milestone
articles.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah praised PM Modi's Independence Day speech as a "Viksit Bharat milestone," outlining a comprehensive roadmap driven by 'nation first' and 'drug-free' spirit, highlighting progress in various sectors.

articles.headline: CAG finds 89% of audited railway stations lack basic amenities
articles.summary: A CAG audit of 512 railway stations revealed that 89% lacked one or more minimum essential amenities, including fans, water coolers, and lavatories. It also found inadequate accessibility for persons with disabilities.

articles.headline: Mahua Moitra seeks LS Speaker's intervention over alleged eviction bid
articles.summary: TMC MP Mahua Moitra wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, seeking intervention after an alleged attempt by West Bengal's Nadia district administration to force her to vacate a Circuit House.

articles.headline: Five killed as vehicle plunges into Chenab River in J&K
articles.summary: Five people were killed in J&K's Kishtwar district after their vehicle skidded off the road and plunged into the Chenab River. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha expressed condolences and directed immediate assistance.

articles.headline: Teenager electrocuted putting up flag at M.P. school
articles.summary: A 17-year-old boy died from electrocution while putting up the national flag for Independence Day celebrations at a private school in Datia, Madhya Pradesh. An FIR was registered against the school management.

articles.headline: Assam government developing comprehensive plan for flood-resilient state, says CM Sarma
articles.summary: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma announced a comprehensive rehabilitation plan for flood-affected families, focusing on rebuilding infrastructure, restoring livelihoods, and creating a flood-resilient state.

articles.headline: Prashant Kishor seeks probe into jail inmate's death in Bihar
articles.summary: Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor met Madhubani SSP, demanding a thorough probe into the death of Roshan Yadav in Rampatti jail, which police claim was suicide, but his family alleges murder.

articles.headline: Nagaland miners' body urges against 'blame game' over Assam floods
articles.summary: The Tuli Area Coal Mining Contractors’ Association urged against blaming Nagaland miners for Assam floods, stating both states suffered from heavy rainfall and advocating for mutual understanding during adversities.

articles.headline: Government cuts export levy on petrol to nil, reduces diesel and ATF duties
articles.summary: The Union government reduced the export duty on petrol to nil and lowered levies on diesel to ₹24 per litre and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) to ₹19.5 per litre, in its fortnightly review to ensure domestic availability.

articles.headline: UPI growth slowing, cash usage quickening as government considers MDR levy
articles.summary: An analysis shows UPI transaction growth is slowing while cash circulation is quickening, even as the government considers a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions, raising concerns about its impact on digital payments.

articles.headline: Top 5 family businesses control over 60% of India's corporate income: Study
articles.summary: A World Bank Economic Review study revealed that India's top five family businesses (Reliance, Adani, Birla, O.P. Jindal, Tata) controlled over 60% of corporate India's income share between 2001 and 2020, despite market liberalization.

articles.headline: NCLAT upholds insolvency order against Nyka Steel personal guarantor
articles.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) upheld an NCLT order initiating insolvency proceedings against the personal guarantor of Nyka Steel, following UCO Bank's plea.

articles.headline: IT rights body flags Wipro's 'prolonged' onboarding delay to Labour Minister
articles.summary: NITES, an IT rights body, complained to Union Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya about Wipro's "prolonged and unexplained delay" in onboarding over 200 students and engineers selected under its Elite Hiring 2025 process.

articles.headline: India's space launch cost highest among major spacefaring nations: Study
articles.summary: A peer-reviewed analysis finds India's per-kilogram space launch cost ($13,302) is the highest among major spacefaring nations, higher than the U.S., Europe, Russia, China, and Japan, attributed to infrequent small rocket launches.

articles.headline: Webb telescope finds supermassive black hole at 'cosmic dawn'
articles.summary: The Webb telescope discovered a rapidly growing supermassive black hole just 660 million years after the Big Bang, shrouded in dense hydrogen gas. Its light-scattering properties suggest early black hole masses may have been overestimated.

articles.headline: TB vaccine offers clue to shaping immunity against Alzheimer’s
articles.summary: A new study suggests the century-old TB vaccine Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) could stimulate the immune system to combat Alzheimer's. It found BCG may trigger "trained immunity" in the central nervous system, influencing amyloid clearance.

articles.headline: Mouse brain protects memories despite significant changes during hibernation
articles.summary: Scientists found mouse brains kept memories intact despite sharp drops in brain activity and loss of over half their hippocampal synapses during hibernation. The brain relies on clustered synapses, which remained protected, to store information.

articles.headline: Switching to an EV almost always better for climate, analysis finds
articles.summary: An analysis of lifecycle emissions found that replacing a functional fossil-fuel vehicle with an EV is almost always better for the climate. The carbon debt from manufacturing a new EV is typically repaid within three years through lower driving emissions.

articles.headline: Google's AI leadership faces challenge with senior tech exits and external competition
articles.summary: Google faces leadership churn as chief scientist Jeff Dean and three senior colleagues leave to co-found an AI startup, Discovery Loop. This exit, funded by Google, signals a shift in AI leadership and highlights competition from faster-moving firms and open-source models.

articles.headline: Anthropic's IPO: Gains and risks in a competitive AI landscape
articles.summary: Anthropic plans a $2 trillion IPO, competing with ChatGPT and open-source models. Risks include Chinese AI advancements, hardware requirements, and the need for continual learning to maintain its edge amid rapidly evolving AI technology and market dynamics.

articles.headline: Centre opposes 'creamy layer' exclusion for SC/ST quotas, citing parliamentary power
articles.summary: The Union government opposes a 'creamy layer' exclusion for SC/ST reservations, arguing such changes require parliamentary action, not judicial direction. The issue arises amid petitions and student movements advocating for income-based reservations and sub-categorization.

articles.headline: Bashar al-Assad sentenced to death in absentia for war crimes
articles.summary: Former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, his brother, cousin, and six others were sentenced to death in absentia by a Damascus court for murder, torture, and war crimes related to the 2011 Daraa uprising crackdown. Russia's asylum complicates extradition.

articles.headline: Nihang Sikhs: Warrior tradition and their presence in public life
articles.summary: The recent attack on Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal by a Nihang sevadar brings the Nihang Sikhs, traditionally 'Guru's army', back into public attention, highlighting their martial tradition, distinct appearance, and decentralized structure.

articles.headline: Devendra Nath Mahto emerges as prominent student agitator in Jharkhand
articles.summary: Devendra Nath Mahto, 33, has become the leading face of Jharkhand's student agitation against alleged irregularities in state recruitment exams. On hunger strike since August 2, he demands CBI inquiry and exam cancellations.

articles.headline: Iran demands release of pilots held in Qatar during West Asia war
articles.summary: Iranian authorities called for the release of three pilots they claim were captured in Qatar after their Su-24 fighter jets crashed during the West Asia war.

articles.headline: Houthi missiles kill four civilians in Yemen’s Mocha port
articles.summary: Yemen’s government reported that Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mocha, killing four civilians, amid escalating hostilities with Saudi-backed opponents.

articles.headline: South Korea proposes talks with North to formally end Korean War
articles.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung proposed talks with North Korea to formally end the Korean War, as Pyongyang deepens ties with Russia and asserts its nuclear state status.

articles.headline: Myanmar verifies 300,000+ Rohingya refugees for repatriation
articles.summary: Myanmar's military-backed government verified over 300,000 Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh camps as former residents, pledging to accept their return once security conditions improve, as the crisis enters its ninth year.

articles.headline: Ukraine attacks Russia’s Samara industrial site and Savasleyka air base
articles.summary: Ukraine struck industrial infrastructure in Russia's Samara region and the Savasleyka air base with long-range aerial attacks, targeting facilities involved in rocket technology and electronics. Russia claimed to shoot down 598 Ukrainian drones.

articles.headline: Israeli air strikes kill at least 11 in southern Lebanon
articles.summary: Israeli air strikes in southern Lebanon killed at least 11 people, including three children, in the deadliest attacks since a June 20 truce. Lebanon's PM criticized the strikes, which Israel said targeted Hezbollah infrastructure.

articles.headline: Taliban celebrates 5 years ruling Afghanistan with rallies, critics decry restrictions
articles.summary: The Taliban regime celebrated five years in power in Afghanistan with street rallies, while critics lamented tightening restrictions on daily life. Their government is only recognized by Russia, with other countries limiting ties due to human rights concerns.

articles.headline: Devdutt Padikkal first Indian to score Test century on Independence Day
articles.summary: Devdutt Padikkal became the first Indian cricketer to score a Test century on Independence Day, notching his maiden hundred against Sri Lanka on the opening day of the Galle Test.

articles.headline: Debutant Nuwantha created chances but was unlucky: Sri Lanka coach Gregory
articles.summary: Sri Lanka's fielding coach Jordan Gregory lauded debutant off-spinner Keshara Nuwantha for creating chances despite being unlucky in the Galle Test, viewing his emergence as a positive for the team.

articles.headline: Sebastian Coe urges LA28 Olympics organizers to work closely with US government
articles.summary: Sebastian Coe advised LA28 Olympic organizers to work closely with the U.S. government, emphasizing the need for political involvement without ceding control, to ensure successful games.

articles.headline: Bulletproof expected to win K. Mahipathi Rao Memorial Golconda Juvenile Million
articles.summary: The three-year-old colt Bulletproof, winner of the Mysore Colts Trial, is favored to win the K. Mahipathi Rao Memorial Golconda Juvenile Million in Sunday's races.

articles.headline: Josh Hazlewood takes 300th Test wicket for Australia
articles.summary: Australian fast bowler Josh Hazlewood claimed his 300th wicket in Test cricket, dismissing Mehidy Hasan Miraz during the first innings against Bangladesh in Darwin.

articles.headline: Sanya Vats loses five-game thriller in Bendigo Open squash semifinals
articles.summary: India's Sanya Vats lost a close five-game match (6-11, 11-8, 9-11, 11-8, 7-11) to Australian third seed Rachael Grinham in the women’s semifinals of the Bendigo Open squash tournament.

articles.headline: Gareth Potts and Kelly Fisher retain Heyball World championships titles
articles.summary: British cueists Gareth Potts and Kelly Fisher successfully defended their titles at the Heyball World championships in Pune. Potts defeated Jordan Shepherd 7-4, and Fisher won a shootout against Waratthanun Sukritthanes.

articles.headline: Manish Ponnamma's hat-trick powers Karnataka to 6-1 hockey win
articles.summary: Skipper Manish Ponnamma scored a hat-trick, leading Karnataka to a dominant 6-1 victory over Uttarakhand in a Division-B contest of the 16th Hockey India junior women’s National championship.

articles.headline: Bangladesh gains control over Australia in Darwin Test
articles.summary: Spinner Mehidy Hasan Miraz took key wickets, reducing Australia to 161 for four and leaving them trailing by 67 runs at stumps on day three, moving Bangladesh closer to a historic victory in the first Test in Darwin.

articles.headline: R. Praggnanandhaa remains in joint second spot at Sinquefield Cup
articles.summary: Indian Grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa drew with Wesley So of the United States in the fifth round of the Sinquefield Cup, maintaining his joint second position with three points.

articles.headline: Japan sweeps all four titles at WSL Shore Temple Classic surfing
articles.summary: Japan dominated the World Surf League (WSL) Shore Temple Classic QS 2000 and Pro Junior (JQS) at Mamallapuram, sweeping all top spots. Ikko Watanabe won the Open men's, and Mirai Ikeda clinched the Open women's titles.

articles.headline: Natural Dye Centre develops eco-friendly paints for idols, Holi
articles.summary: PJTSAU's Natural Dye Processing and Incubation Centre in Hyderabad is developing biodegradable paints and Holi powders from natural dyes. This initiative offers safer alternatives to synthetic colors, reducing environmental pollution and health risks associated with idol painting and festival celebrations.

articles.headline: PM Modi Unveils Seven-Pillar 'Viksit Bharat' 2047 Plan
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on India's 80th Independence Day at Red Fort, unveiled 'Saptdhara', a seven-pillar roadmap for 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047, focusing on manufacturing, agriculture, tech, infrastructure, defense, green energy, and soft power. He urged passing the women's reservation bill, announced a 2036 Olympics sports prodigy hunt, emphasized self-reliance, and invited public-private participation.

articles.headline: Arunachal Rains: 5 Army Personnel Missing, 5 Dead Amid Floods, Landslides
articles.summary: Heavy monsoon rains caused flash floods and landslides in Arunachal Pradesh. Five army personnel from 5th Grenadiers are missing in Dibang Valley after being swept away near the LAC. Four workers were trapped at a road construction site, with two rescued. At least five people died and several others are unaccounted for after three days of incidents. Rescue efforts by NDRF/SDRF are hampered by bad weather and difficult terrain.

articles.headline: Iran Rejects Trump's Claim to Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Former US President Donald Trump stated he would declare the Strait of Hormuz US territory if elected. Iran's foreign ministry rejected this, asserting the vital global oil transit point remains under Iranian sovereignty and warned against US encroachment. Analysts clarified the waterway is governed by international law and cannot be unilaterally claimed, emphasizing it will be opened/closed under Iran's command.

articles.headline: Powerful 7.7 Magnitude Quake Kills At Least 47 in Indonesia
articles.summary: A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck eastern Indonesia's Flores region, killing at least 47 people and injuring hundreds. The quake and over 235 aftershocks, up to 6.2 magnitude, destroyed thousands of homes and damaged infrastructure in Ngada and Riung. Rescue efforts are hampered by landslides, power outages, and cut-off remote villages, with the death toll expected to rise. A brief tsunami warning was issued but later withdrawn.

articles.headline: Govt Launches Foreign Asset Disclosure Scheme For Small Taxpayers
articles.summary: The Union finance ministry launched FAST-DS, a one-time amnesty scheme for small taxpayers to disclose undocumented foreign assets/income. Eligible individuals can regularize assets by paying 60% tax (30% tax + 30% penalty) without further penalties or prosecution. Effective until December 31, the scheme aims to broaden the tax base and reduce litigation for minor overseas holdings.

articles.headline: BCI Chief Apologises After NALSAR Convocation Controversy
articles.summary: Bar Council of India Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra issued a formal apology to law students after a controversy at a NALSAR University convocation. The row stemmed from comments regarding student protests against the CJI's appearance and professional conduct. Mishra stated his intent was to guide with 'patience and sensitivity' rather than cause offense or hurt the legal academic community.

articles.headline: TN CM Vijay Pledges Corruption-Free Governance, People's Welfare
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu CM C. Joseph Vijay, in his first Independence Day speech, pledged a "corruption-free government" focused on absolute people's welfare, rejecting caste and money power. He announced increased financial aid for freedom fighters, expanded the breakfast scheme to more schools, and vowed cooperation with the Centre while opposing anti-State policies.

articles.headline: AP CM Naidu Pledges 'Swarna Andhra 2047' Vision
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh CM N. Chandrababu Naidu highlighted "destruction to development" in his 26-month tenure, noting progress in Amaravati and reviving ₹8,000 crore in welfare schemes. He urged citizens' collective resolve to build a "Healthy, Wealthy and Happy Swarna Andhra by 2047," aligning with PM Modi's Viksit Bharat vision, and transforming the state into a global investment hub.

articles.headline: Three Suspected Poachers Killed in Karnataka Forest Encounter
articles.summary: Three suspected poachers were killed in an alleged exchange of fire with forest officials in Karnataka's Chamarajanagar district. Authorities claimed the men carried illegal firearms and venison, while local villagers disputed, alleging they were innocent farmers. A magisterial inquiry has been ordered to investigate the circumstances leading to the encounter in the protected zone.

articles.headline: Telangana Launches Digital Smart Ration Cards for 3.4 Crore Families
articles.summary: Telangana CM A. Revanth Reddy and Deputy CM Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka launched Digital Smart Ration Cards to digitize the PDS for 3.4 crore beneficiaries (10.5 million families). The PVC cards with QR codes and enhanced security aim to ensure fine-quality rice, prevent fraud, and expand commodity offerings, with new cards sanctioned for eligible families.

articles.headline: PM Announces Free AI-Enabled Coaching for 1 Crore Youth via SATHEE
articles.summary: The Prime Minister announced free online coaching via AI-enabled SATHEE for 1 crore youth (10 million students) preparing for competitive exams like NEET, JEE, and CUET. This initiative, also including AI training, aims to reduce financial burden and provide equal opportunities for poor and middle-class students by leveraging India's digital platforms nationwide.

articles.headline: India Dominates Wales 3-1 in Hockey World Cup Opener
articles.summary: The Indian men's hockey team began its FIH World Cup campaign in Amstelveen with a 3-1 victory over Wales. Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored two goals, with Mandeep Singh and Akashdeep Singh also contributing. India dominated possession, converting penalty corners, and sits atop Pool D. The team aims for its first World Cup medal since 1975, with coach Craig Fulton emphasizing defensive solidity.

articles.headline: Tejasvi Dahiya Leads South Delhi Superstarz to DPL Victory
articles.summary: Stand-in skipper Tejasvi Dahiya's unbeaten 60 off 29 balls led South Delhi Superstarz to a six-wicket victory over New Delhi Tigers, chasing 218 in the Delhi Premier League opener. Ayush Badoni also contributed 35 runs. The T20 league aims to provide a platform for local Delhi talent to showcase their skills.

articles.headline: Padikkal's Maiden Century Puts India in Control of Galle Test
articles.summary: Devdutt Padikkal scored a masterful maiden Test century (131* off 178 balls) on Day 1 of the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, putting India in a commanding position. Supported by KL Rahul (77 retired hurt) and Yashasvi Jaiswal (32), India reached 288/2. Sri Lankan bowlers struggled on a rain-affected pitch, with Prabath Jayasuriya taking one wicket during the afternoon session.

articles.headline: PM Modi Warns Nation Against 'Dimagi Naxals'
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day speech at the Red Fort, warned against 'Dimagi Naxals' (intellectual Naxals), stating they mislead youth and spread anarchy. He urged the nation to identify and isolate them to protect India’s future and development, while also addressing youth anxieties by promising AI skilling for 1 crore youth and free online coaching.

articles.headline: Padikkal's Maiden Century Bolsters India's Test No. 3 Claim
articles.summary: Karnataka batsman Devdutt Padikkal scored an unbeaten 131 in a warm-up match against Sri Lanka in Galle, making a strong case for India's Test No. 3 spot. His maiden century, an 184-ball knock including 13 fours and 1 six, helped India reach 288/2 and highlights his emergence as a key player for India's Test middle order, putting pressure on selectors.

articles.headline: Omar Abdullah Demands J&K's Special Status Return, Cites PoK Unrest
articles.summary: J&K CM Omar Abdullah, in his Independence Day speech, demanded the return of J&K's special status (indirectly Article 370), advocating for stronger federalism and states' rights. He cited recent violent protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir as vindication of his grandfather's 1947 decision to join India, highlighting the democratic framework compared to the lack of constitutional guarantees across the LoC.

articles.headline: BJP Accuses Sonia Gandhi of Disrupting National Song
articles.summary: A political row erupted after the BJP accused Congress leader Sonia Gandhi of trying to stop the full rendition of 'Vande Mataram' at an Independence Day event, and demanded an apology. The Congress denied the claims, stating Gandhi was merely seeking a chair for party president Mallikarjun Kharge. The incident sparked heated social media debates.

articles.headline: PSG Signs Spain World Cup Star Ferran Torres from Barcelona
articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain completed the signing of Spanish World Cup star Ferran Torres from Barcelona for a reported €50-53 million. Torres, who scored in the World Cup final, signed a five-year contract as part of PSG's strategy to revamp its attacking lineup under manager Luis Enrique for the upcoming Ligue 1 season.

articles.headline: Thousands Attend Red Fort I-Day Amidst Tight Security
articles.summary: Thousands attended India's 80th Independence Day celebrations at Red Fort, with many first-time visitors sharing emotional experiences despite pass issues. Over 25,000 security personnel, including NSG and rapid response teams, and 1,000 AI-enabled CCTV cameras were deployed, ensuring extensive security in and around the venue and surrounding areas.

articles.headline: Attack on Sukhbir Badal Called "Political Conspiracy"
articles.summary: SAD MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal termed the 'kirpan' attack on her husband, party chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, by a 'Nihang sevadar' a "well-planned political conspiracy" aimed at disrupting peace in Punjab. The incident highlights the growing threat from radical elements exploiting a leadership vacuum due to SAD's weakening support base.

articles.headline: Coach Kotak: Rahul Fit, Praises Padikkal's Adaptability
articles.summary: India's batting coach Sitanshu Kotak confirmed KL Rahul, who retired hurt with cramps during the Galle Test, is "absolutely fine" and available to play, praising his adaptability across formats. Kotak also expressed delight with Devdutt Padikkal's maiden Test century, commending his improved back-foot game and ability to adapt to conditions after training at NCA.

articles.headline: Chinese Shuttlers Face Diminishing Dominance at Badminton Worlds
articles.summary: Chinese badminton players are showing diminishing dominance at the Badminton World Championships in New Delhi, with no women's singles champion since 2011 and only Shi Yuqi defending a title. This highlights a global power shift, with Chinese shuttlers acknowledging local conditions like "drift" and "weather" during the tournament, amid high expectations and India's home-court intensity.
